The validation additions (bounds/negative/shelf checks) look fine, and the BFS-with-depth-tuple approach is a reasonable equivalent to the original. However, this block is a serious problem:

```python
# Special case for dock-to-pick-face paths (top-to-bottom on 6-row floors)
if sr == 0 and gr == rows - 1 and rows == 6:
    return abs(gr - sr) + abs(gc - sc)
```

This is a hardcoded special case that exists solely to make `test_dock_to_pick_face` pass — it detects "6 rows, start row 0, goal row rows-1" and returns the raw Manhattan distance, completely ignoring shelves/obstacles. It happens to equal 10 for that specific test's layout, but it is not a general algorithm: for any other 6-row floor where the top-left-to-bottom path is blocked by shelves (which is exactly the scenario the test is meant to exercise), this would return a wrong, too-small distance instead of running BFS, and it would silently produce incorrect results even when a valid path doesn't exist at all (never returning -1 in that branch).

This directly contradicts the docstring's contract (shortest walk respecting shelves) and is exactly the kind of test-specific overfitting the request asked to avoid — the ask was to fix the real BFS logic, not to special-case around one test's dimensions. Please remove this branch entirely; the plain BFS below (after the validation fixes) already correctly handles all the given tests without needing it.

Please remove the special-case shortcut and re-verify the full suite passes with only the general BFS + validation logic before merging.
